title: Heterogeneous SLO firebreaks for model rollouts
creator: Aisha Patel
description: Implement an automated rollback trigger system that uses heterogeneous SLO "firebreaks" across latency, error rate, token cost, and throughput for model rollouts. Objectives: reduce noisy aborts, avoid over-reverting during transient spikes, and provide explainable rollback decisions for product and SRE stakeholders.
rationale: Current canary abort logic applies uniform thresholds and simple deltas. That causes both false positives (transient infra spikes triggering rollbacks) and false negatives (token-cost regressions slowly erode margins). We need a flexible, cohort-aware guardrail that treats different signals asymmetrically and reasons about confidence before evacuating traffic.
design_notes: Key principles: 1) heterogeneous thresholds per signal and per cohort (e.g., premium vs free) 2) asymmetric hysteresis — easier to open a gate when severe regressions but harder to close based on single-sample noise 3) Bayesian change-point scoring for confidence estimation 4) cost-aware decisions that weight token-cost regressions differently when traffic is heavily cached 5) explicit tie-breaker policies and an operator-visible score with provenance for audits.
solution_sketch: We will compute a per-deployment 'evacuation_score' = weighted sum of normalized signal deltas where weights are configurable by project and inferred from historical impact. Each signal uses a two-component detector: short-window anomaly detector (synthetic median absolute deviation) and medium-window Bayesian change-point posterior. The evacuation_score is thresholded into three bands: advisory, throttle (reduce new traffic), and evacuate (auto-rollback). To avoid thrash, we apply cohort hysteresis: minimum dwell time, traffic-aware debouncing, and an emergency override channel. Telemetry and reasoning context (metric deltas, confidence, raw time-series) are attached to rollout events.
rollout_plan: Phase 1 (dev): implement detectors and scoring in runtime-metrics-service behind feature flag. Phase 2 (alpha): enable advisory band for selected internal customers. Phase 3 (beta): allow automated throttle decisions (traffic split reductions). Phase 4 (GA): enable auto-evacuate for P1 customers with configurable policies and human-in-loop for P0. Each phase runs at least two weeks and includes synthetic load tests and cost regressions.
metrics: Primary signals: p95 latency (ms), error rate (5xx+client-fallback-%), token-cost-per-response (tokens/response), throughput (requests/s). Secondary: cache hit ratio, kv-cache-miss-rate, cold-starts/min. For each signal we compute baseline (rolling 7-day median) and short-window (5m) and medium-window (60m) deltas.
monitoring_queries: SLO alert query: increase(token_cost_total[1h]) > (1.15 * increase(token_cost_baseline[1h])) /* token cost inflation guard */
acceptance_criteria: Detectors produce an evacuation_score for every canary rollout event and surface it in rollout UI
Advisory band shown in Console for at least three internal rollouts and feedback collected
Throttle band can reduce new traffic automatically in alpha and reverses after confidence drop is below hysteresis threshold
Auto-evacuate triggers only when evacuation_score >= evacuation_threshold AND Bayesian posterior confidence >= 0.95
All auto-evacuate actions produce an audit record with metric excerpts and links to raw time-series
Automated tests simulate transient infra spike and ensure no auto-evacuate for single short-window anomaly
tasks: Create metric adapters in runtime-metrics-service for normalized deltas
Implement short-window MAD detector and medium-window Bayesian change-point module
Add evacuation_score computation and policy config to rollout controller
Expose advisory/throttle/evacuate bands to Console with explanation text
Add audit logging and automations to Deployment Events stream
Run synthetic load/cost regression test-suite and record results
Write runbook for SRE and PM on interpreting evacuation_score and manual override
